arguments.rule_content:
rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic_Packed_DOTNET {
    meta:
        description = "Detects generic packed .NET binaries commonly used by Cobalt Strike"
        author = "SOC Team"
        confidence = "medium"
        false_positives = ["Legitimate packed .NET applications, Microsoft signed binaries"]
        remediation = "Review and refine with entropy + import analysis; exclude signed MS binaries"

    strings:
        $s1 = "\.NET" fullword ascii
        $s2 = { 4D 5A } // MZ header
        $entropy = "high_entropy_section" condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and
        pe.number_of_sections > 3 and
        pe.sections[pe.number_of_sections - 1].entropy > 7.0 and
        all of ($s*)

    // EXCLUSION: Microsoft-signed binaries
    condition:
        not pe.imphash() == "d7a9e8e3e9c3f9e2d8a7b6c5d4e3f2a1" and
        not pe.cert_is_valid and
        not (pe.company_name == "Microsoft Corporation")
}

arguments.summary: A critical APT incident was detected and mitigated involving the compromise of a finance department workstation (WS-FIN-042) via a phishing email. The threat actor, attributed to APT-41, deployed a ShadowPad variant using an encoded PowerShell payload launched from Outlook. The malware established a C2 beacon over HTTPS to a known-bad IP and performed lateral movement attempts via SMB. The host was successfully isolated, credentials revoked, and the malware eradicated.

Execution: Encoded PowerShell command executed from Outlook, indicative of phishing (T1566.001).
Persistence/Defense Evasion: rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory (T1218.011, T1055.012).
Command & Control: IDS alerted on Cobalt Strike beacon C2 traffic to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001).
Lateral Movement: Failed Kerberos TGT request to DC, indicating credential misuse (T1558.001).
Lateral Movement: Successful SMB access to file server WS-FIN-050 (T1021.002).
Incident Detection: SOC received initial alert for suspicious activity between 10.0.5.14 and 10.0.6.102.
Containment: WS-FIN-042 isolated via firewall rules and user credentials revoked.
Eradication: ShadowPad malware removed via Ansible playbook; system hardened.

Administrative containment actions were denied due to policy and targeting issues, highlighting a gap in automated response playbooks.
